newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish agency sees '96 grain harvest at 24-5 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Polish agency sees '96 grain harvest at 24-5 mln T.

text.p: The Polish government's food market regulator, the Agriculture Marget Agency (ARR), expects this year's grain harvest to be between 24 and 25 million tonnes, down from 25.9 million in 1995, ARR said on Thursday.
"The grain harvest in 1996 is presently estimated at 24 to 25 million tonnes, which is about one to two million tonnes less than last year," the agency said in a statement.
It said domestic grain consumption would decrease by about 1.5 million tonnes in 1996/97 because of falling demand for feed grains, especially for pigs.
It said demand for food grains would remain basically flat from last year.
The ARR added that 1996/97 demand would again exceed domestic grain supply and Poland would have to import to fill the gap.
"Domestic grain supply will be aided by grain imports, but the imports will be smaller than last growing season," it said.
It said the price of wheat, at about 600 zlotys per tonne in mid-September, would reach 630-660 zlotys by the end of the year, while rye prices would rise to 400-420 zlotys from about 380 last week.

The agency expected the price of wheat to rise to 650-690 zlotys in March and 670-720 in June. It forecast rye prices at the end of the first quarter of 1997 at 420-450 zlotys/tonne and at the end of the second 430-460.
